heuristics.title: The Master Directionality Rule
heuristics.rule: ALL nucleic acid synthesis (DNA replication, RNA transcription) occurs strictly in the 5' -> 3' direction; the template strand is read in the 3' -> 5' direction.
heuristics.explanation: Incoming nucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs or NTPs) provide energy via hydrolysis of their alpha-beta phosphoanhydride bond, joining their 5'-phosphate to the free 3'-OH group of the growing chain.

heuristics.title: Proofreading Exonuclease Directionality
heuristics.rule: Replicative proofreading exonuclease activity runs strictly in the 3' -> 5' direction.
heuristics.explanation: When an incorrect nucleotide is inserted, the polymerase pauses, transfers the mismatched 3' end to the proofreading exonuclease site, removes the nucleotide backward (3'->5'), and resumes forward 5'->3' synthesis.

heuristics.title: The Primer Rule: DNA vs. RNA Polymerases
heuristics.rule: DNA polymerases CANNOT initiate synthesis de novo and strictly require a pre-existing 3'-OH primer; RNA polymerases initiate synthesis de novo without a primer.
heuristics.explanation: Because DNA polymerases require a primer, DNA replication requires Primase (a specialized RNA polymerase) to lay down an RNA primer before DNA synthesis can commence.

heuristics.title: DNA Repair Human Deficiency Syndromes
heuristics.rule:
* Xeroderma Pigmentosum (XP) -> Defect in Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER) (cannot repair UV thymine dimers)
* Lynch Syndrome (HNPCC) -> Defect in Mismatch Repair (MMR) (MSH2, MLH1)
* Ataxia-Telangiectasia (AT) -> Defect in ATM kinase (detects double-strand DNA breaks)
* Fanconi Anemia / BRCA1/2 -> Defect in Homologous Recombination repair.
heuristics.explanation: High-yield medical exam associations connecting specific DNA repair enzymes to hereditary cancer syndromes.
